manualRef: Pairs with the Arduino Projects plan: Traffic Light, project 1 of 8. Pin map and code live in the plan, not in this file.

parts.name: Arduino Uno
parts.notes: USB port faces left. Pins 8, 9, 10 drive the three LEDs.

parts.name: Half-size breadboard
parts.notes: Rails run along the long edges. Red rail is 5V, blue rail is GND.

parts.name: Red LED, 5 mm
parts.notes: Long leg is +. Goes to pin 8 through a resistor.

parts.name: Yellow LED, 5 mm
parts.notes: Long leg is +. Goes to pin 9 through a resistor.

parts.name: Green LED, 5 mm
parts.notes: Long leg is +. Goes to pin 10 through a resistor.

parts.name: 220 ohm resistor
parts.notes: Red-red-brown-gold bands. One per LED, in series.

parts.name: 220 ohm resistor
parts.notes: Red-red-brown-gold bands. One per LED, in series.

parts.name: 220 ohm resistor
parts.notes: Red-red-brown-gold bands. One per LED, in series.

parts.name: USB cable
parts.notes: Must carry data, not charge-only. Charge-only cables are the most common failure.

steps.text: One Uno, one breadboard, three LEDs, three resistors, four jumper wires, one USB cable. Count them before you start. A missing resistor at step 4 costs more time than counting now.
steps.title: What is in the box

steps.text: Set the Uno on the left of your workspace, USB port facing left. Nothing plugs in yet.
steps.title: Place the Arduino Uno

steps.text: Breadboard goes to the right of the Uno, rails along the top and bottom edges. Red rail is 5V, blue rail is GND.
steps.title: Place the breadboard

steps.text: Red left, yellow middle, green right. Long leg is +. Short leg goes to the GND rail. Push them in until the plastic base touches the board.
steps.tip: If an LED is backwards it will not light and nothing else is wrong. Flip it before you rewire anything.
steps.title: Seat the LEDs

steps.text: One 220 ohm resistor in series with each LED, between the Uno pin and the long leg. Red-red-brown-gold bands.
steps.title: Add one resistor per LED

steps.text: Red wire pin 8 to red LED, yellow wire pin 9 to yellow LED, green wire pin 10 to green LED, black wire GND rail to Uno GND. Then plug in the USB cable. Data cable, not charge-only.
steps.title: Wire it up and plug in USB

steps.text: Upload the Traffic Light sketch. Red 3 seconds, yellow 1 second, green 3 seconds, then repeat. If one LED stays dark, check its resistor and its long leg first.
steps.tip: Three in a row. One working cycle is luck. Three is a demo.
steps.title: Upload and test

subtitle: The starter build from the AA8 Arduino plan. 2 x 1.5 hour sessions, USB power only, no soldering.
